<reason>CON won a competitive clash by taking the motion as written: a sticky, system-level ad-and-tracker filter is a prior commercial cut, not restored owner control. PRO’s owner-default principle and consent-theater case were strong, but never neutralized the live-veto/list problem, first-party platform moat, or how an audible opt-out survives after the funding stack is stripped. PRO’s clipped R2 and weaker answers to those pressures left CON’s “silent poorer web” comparison easier to vote on.</reason>
<best_rebuttal>CON’s prior-filter exchange: after robust OS blocking, nothing carries a publisher’s ask the way cookie banners on a still-funded page do, so PRO’s “opt-out / make the case directly” claim is not matching reversibility.</best_rebuttal>
